Let’s dive into Chapter 9: Philanthropy, Legacy, and the Meaning of Wealth.
As the years rolled by and his snowball kept growing, our investor started to look at wealth from a whole new angle.
He realized something powerful—money isn’t the finish line. It’s just a tool. What really matters is what you choose to do with it, and the difference you can make with the resources you’ve built.
He thought back to the very first time he gave away a significant sum. That moment was both thrilling and humbling. He could actually see the positive change—lives touched, doors opened, real opportunities created. Suddenly, he understood: the deepest sense of satisfaction didn’t come from watching his fortune grow, but from sharing it.
He began to wonder about legacy. What would he leave behind? How did he want to be remembered? More than anything, he wanted to use his resources to tackle some of the world’s biggest challenges—to support education, improve health, and create opportunities for those who needed them the most.
Humility played a big part in this journey. He knew luck had helped him along the way, and that plenty of talented and hardworking people just hadn’t caught the same breaks. That realization sparked a deeper desire to give back, to help level the playing field for future generations.
Philanthropy didn’t stay a solo act for long. It became a family affair—he brought his kids and close friends into the fold, inviting them to think carefully about how their giving could have the greatest impact. They focused on supporting organizations that lined up with their values—groups that were transparent, effective, and committed to making a long-term difference.
He also became a voice for responsible giving. He pushed back against waste and inefficiency, encouraging others to approach philanthropy with the same discipline and attention to detail that he used in investing. After all, shouldn’t every dollar do the most good it possibly can?
Over time, his whole relationship with wealth shifted. He stopped thinking of himself as the owner of his fortune, and started seeing himself as a steward—someone who’s responsible for using what he has to help others. He urged those around him to adopt the same mindset: see wealth not as a trophy, but as a way to serve.
